encounters.cc: Six-month history of episodic facial flushing, watery diarrhea, and wheezing episodes.

lines: Six-month history of episodic facial flushing, watery diarrhea, and wheezing episodes.
She reports that the flushing episodes are intense, last for about 10 minutes, and are sometimes accompanied by a feeling of warmth and palpitations.
Her diarrhea is watery, occurs 3-4 times a day, and is not associated with any particular food intake.
She also mentions occasional shortness of breath that seems to be unrelated to physical activity.
She has a past medical history of asthma.
She takes for which she uses an albuterol inhaler as needed.
- Albuterol HFA inhaler 90 mcg, 2 puffs every 4-6 hours as needed for wheezing
- Fluticasone propionate/salmeterol diskus 250/50 mcg, 1 inhalation twice daily
- Mometasone nasal spray 2 sprays in each nostril twice daily
- Montelukast 10 mg orally once daily at bedtime
- Octreotide LAR 30 mg intramuscularly every 4 weeks
- Cetirizine 10 mg orally once daily as needed
- Epinephrine auto-injector 0.3 mg, inject intramuscularly as needed for anaphylaxis
Ibuprofen (anaphylaxis), Aspirin (anaphylaxis), Shellfish (anaphylaxis), Tree pollen (seasonal allergic rhinitis)
On physical examination, she appears malnourished with evidence of dermatitis on sun-exposed areas of her skin.
Cardiac auscultation reveals a high-pitched, early diastolic murmur best heard along the right sternal border.
- Complete Blood Count (CBC): Within normal limits

encounters.cc: Progressive shortness of breath, fatigue, and unintentional weight loss over the past month with new left foot numbness.

lines: Progressive shortness of breath, fatigue, and unintentional weight loss over the past month with new left foot numbness.
The patient, with severe persistent asthma and eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis, returns for follow-up one year after her initial Endocrinology presentation.
She has a 10-year history of asthma that had previously been well controlled but has recently become more severe, requiring frequent use of her rescue inhaler.
She also reports numbness and tingling in her left foot, which began a few weeks ago.
- Albuterol HFA inhaler 90 mcg, 2 puffs every 4-6 hours as needed for wheezing
- Fluticasone propionate/salmeterol diskus 250/50 mcg, 1 inhalation twice daily
- Mometasone nasal spray 2 sprays in each nostril twice daily
- Montelukast 10 mg orally once daily at bedtime
- Octreotide LAR 30 mg intramuscularly every 4 weeks
- Cetirizine 10 mg orally once daily as needed
- Epinephrine auto-injector 0.3 mg, inject intramuscularly as needed for anaphylaxis
Ibuprofen (anaphylaxis), Aspirin (anaphylaxis), Shellfish (anaphylaxis), Tree pollen (seasonal allergic rhinitis)
Scattered expiratory wheezes and decreased sensation over the dorsum of her left foot
High eosinophils and an elevated ESR.
A sural nerve biopsy reveals necrotizing inflammation of small vessels with surrounding eosinophils and granulomas.

encounters.cc: Acute generalized urticaria, severe dyspnea, and lightheadedness immediately after shellfish ingestion with biphasic reaction requiring second epinephrine dose.

lines: Acute generalized urticaria, severe dyspnea, and lightheadedness immediately after shellfish ingestion with biphasic reaction requiring second epinephrine dose.

The patient with severe persistent asthma, aspirin-exacerbated respiratory disease, and prior emergency department presentations for NSAID-induced respiratory reactions presents after shellfish ingestion, to which she states she has a known allergy.
She is administered intramuscular epinephrine, after which her symptoms improve significantly.
However, 1 hour later, her symptoms recur with worsening respiratory distress and hypotension.
She receives a second dose of epinephrine with improvement.
She has a history of asthma and eczema.
- Albuterol HFA inhaler 90 mcg, 2 puffs every 4-6 hours as needed for wheezing
- Fluticasone propionate/salmeterol diskus 250/50 mcg, 1 inhalation twice daily
- Mometasone nasal spray 2 sprays in each nostril twice daily
- Montelukast 10 mg orally once daily at bedtime
- Octreotide LAR 30 mg intramuscularly every 4 weeks
- Cetirizine 10 mg orally once daily as needed
- Epinephrine auto-injector 0.3 mg, inject intramuscularly as needed for anaphylaxis
Ibuprofen (anaphylaxis), Aspirin (anaphylaxis), Shellfish (anaphylaxis), Tree pollen (seasonal allergic rhinitis)
On examination, her blood pressure is 85/50 mmHg, heart rate is 120 beats per minute, respiratory rate is 28 breaths per minute, and oxygen saturation is 88% on room air.
She has diffuse wheezing on auscultation, facial angioedema, and a diffuse, raised, erythematous rash.
- Basic metabolic panel: Within normal limits
